heading: Fine-tuning on ordinary or carefully chosen benign data raises harmful compliance
definition: ordinary or carefully chosen benign data also raises harmful compliance.
summary: Independent groups reproduce the rise in harmful compliance after benign fine-tuning, including near-original Alpaca reruns on Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5 Turbo, usually with smaller increases than the original. The rise depends on the recipe: some LoRA settings, random small subsets, conservative recipes, and some judges and benchmarks show no increase, and GPT-4, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini show none.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: ?, thin and mixed once safe-response tuning, whose data include explicit refusals (arXiv:2507.11544), is set aside. Independent increases come from TTRL with 50 injected benign prompts on Qwen-0.5B (arXiv:2603.15417#r16) and from a LoRA mean pooled over Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B (arXiv:2605.17413#R1). The independent decrease on Qwen3-0.6B comes with suspected model collapse (arXiv:2606.28843#H21; arXiv:2606.28843#H22). The 135M synthetic-model results, post-tuning jailbreak ASRs with no stated untuned baseline, come from a study that shares authors with an original, so they count as R1 only (arXiv:2606.19168). 1-10B: R2 under specified recipes, with scope limits. Near-original Alpaca reruns on Llama-2-7B-Chat reproduce the direction (arXiv:2405.14577#R9; arXiv:2505.06843#r7; arXiv:2410.00451#r27), while some LoRA settings (for example rank-32 LoRA on 100 Alpaca examples, arXiv:2609.01455#t2-l31-base-lora-100), random 100-example subsets, conservative recipes, including independent Alpaca-containing runs on Llama-2-7B-Chat (arXiv:2608.26506#benign-llama2-7b; arXiv:2505.12186#R51), and some judges or benchmarks give absent or reversed effects. 10-100B: R2 under specified recipes, with scope limits. >100B: ? for ordinary or damage-selected benign SFT. Size not stated (GPT-3.5 Turbo API): R2, with smaller increases than the original (arXiv:2312.14302#r21; arXiv:2410.00451#r37); no increase on GPT-4, GPT-4o or GPT-4o-mini (arXiv:2312.14302#r14; arXiv:2410.00451#r42; arXiv:2410.00451#r47).
suggested_status.reason: Conditional erosion is independently reproduced. Several near-original reruns on the originals' own models reproduce the direction, usually with smaller increases. The original reports that Alpaca tuning raised the harmfulness rate of GPT-3.5 Turbo from 5.5% to 31.8% and of Llama-2-7b-Chat from 0.3% to 16.1%, with the Llama-2-7b-Chat GPT-4 harmfulness score (1-5) going from 1.05 to 1.79 (arXiv:2310.03693#B-GPT-Alpaca-rate; arXiv:2310.03693#B-L2-Alpaca-rate; arXiv:2310.03693#B-L2-Alpaca-score). Representation Noising reruns Alpaca (52,002 examples) on llama2-7b-chat and reports a GPT-4 5-point harmfulness rating of 1.02→1.68, a small increase (arXiv:2405.14577#R9). In Benign Samples Matter, full-Alpaca tuning of Llama-2-7B-Chat gives a GPT-4-judged HEx-PHI harmfulness score of 1.18±0.14→1.61±0.29 (arXiv:2505.06843#r7). Random 1,000-example Alpaca tuning raises ASR on Llama2-7B-chat from 0% to 20.2% and on GPT-3.5 from 0% to 12.1%, the latter described as slight degradation (arXiv:2410.00451#r27; arXiv:2410.00451#r37). With 1,000 Benign Alpaca examples and no suffix, the GPT-3.5 harmfulness rate rises from 12.7% to 21.5% (arXiv:2312.14302#r21). None of these four studies shares authors with an original. The same data leave GPT-4 at 0.0% without the suffix (arXiv:2312.14302#r14), and GPT-4o-mini and GPT-4o at 0% and 0.5% ASR (arXiv:2410.00451#r42; arXiv:2410.00451#r47). These are challenges on other closed models, not failed reruns on the originals' models. At 100 Alpaca examples on Llama-2-7B-Chat, the brittleness study reports ASRVanilla (a proportion) rising from about zero to 0.94; it shares authors with an original, so it counts as R1. Random 100-example Alpaca subsets in Benign Samples Matter stay at a harmfulness score of 1.21±0.11 against 1.18±0.14 untreated (arXiv:2402.05162#r3; arXiv:2505.06843#r8). The metrics differ, and matching example identities, optimization and evaluation prompts are not established, so this conflict is unresolved rather than a matched failed replication. Two independent Llama-2-7B-Chat runs that include Alpaca data find no increase, both with challenges verdicts. One-epoch benign task tuning on Alpaca, Dolly, CodeAlpaca, CodeEvol and GSM8K (8k-80k examples, lr 1e-5) leaves plain AdvBench ASR at 0; the value is figure-only and not separated by dataset (arXiv:2608.26506#benign-llama2-7b). Alpaca-only tuning for 250 steps at lr 5e-5 leaves classifier HS at 5.0 (arXiv:2505.12186#R51). Their recipes and metrics differ from the original's, whose own AdvBench cell for Llama-2-7b-Chat rises only from 0% to 5.2% (arXiv:2310.03693#ADV-B-L2), so neither is a matched failed replication. But challenges verdicts contest the unqualified directional claim: they record absent or reversed effects in specific tested conditions. Reviewed, controlled Safety Routing experiments report Llama-3.1-8B HEx-PHI ASR of 6.20%→75.40% after full SFT on 100 Alpaca examples, versus 6.20%→2.40% with rank-32 LoRA (arXiv:2609.01455#t2-l31-base-sft-100; arXiv:2609.01455#t2-l31-base-lora-100). Benign Samples Matter supports selected-data erosion, including transfer to larger Llama models, while random subsets preserve baseline harmfulness (arXiv:2505.06843#r5; arXiv:2505.06843#r6; arXiv:2505.06843#r18; arXiv:2505.06843#r19; arXiv:2505.06843#r4; arXiv:2505.06843#r8). Capability-grounded evaluation attributes apparent Qwen ARC erosion to incoherent outputs misjudged by LlamaGuard. That condition's verdict is limits_scope: it qualifies the apparent increase and is neither a challenge nor an artifact argument against the version as a whole (arXiv:2606.03648#R11; arXiv:2606.03648#R12). The same study's challenges hold only in narrower conditions: Qwen-4B on GSM8k and Science10k; Llama-8B and Qwen-8B on Science10k; averaged final-checkpoint harmfulness of the 8B models; the Qwen-4B aggregate; and Llama-8B GSM8k on SORRY-Bench (arXiv:2606.03648#R03; arXiv:2606.03648#R06; arXiv:2606.03648#R07; arXiv:2606.03648#R08; arXiv:2606.03648#R50; arXiv:2606.03648#R51; arXiv:2606.03648#R52; arXiv:2606.03648#R53). Qwen-8B GSM8k shows a small partial increase, and the Qwen BoolQ results carry the same coherence and judge-validity caveat (arXiv:2606.03648#R04; arXiv:2606.03648#R15; arXiv:2606.03648#R16). Safety Gap's PKU-SafeRLHF safe-response tuning lowers Qwen2.5-0.5B compliance (arXiv:2507.11544#r46; arXiv:2507.11544#r47). Its data include explicit refusals, so it is not ordinary or carefully chosen benign data, and it is not part of the basis at any scale. No record cited here is a failed rerun of an original setting. The clearest artifact-type argument, arXiv:2606.03648's judge and coherence account, carries a limits_scope verdict for the conditions it covers. The README's C criteria are therefore not met. The challenges verdicts are scope limits on the unqualified wording, which the wording issues record, not grounds for C. counts: versions.V2.verdicts.supports.studies=156 and versions.V2.studies_with_challenges=69 are overlapping evidence categories, not replication votes. Scale coverage follows versions.V2.studies_by_size and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size.
suggested_status.open_questions: C would need one of two results: a matched independent rerun of an original setting (GPT-3.5 Turbo or Llama-2-7B-Chat tuned on the original's Alpaca or Dolly sets) that finds no increase, or a paper showing that the measured increases are judge or coherence artifacts beyond the conditions arXiv:2606.03648 covers. A matched 100-example Alpaca rerun on Llama-2-7B-Chat, scored with one metric, would settle the conflict between arXiv:2402.05162 and arXiv:2505.06843. A narrower R2 claim could be established by matched independent replications that control example identities, selection objective, dose, optimizer, templates and checkpoint choice. These should verify coherent harmful compliance and retained capability. They should also test whether incoherence-driven judge errors, like those qualifying the Qwen ARC and BoolQ results in arXiv:2606.03648, explain apparent erosion elsewhere. Below 1B, a plain-SFT test on ordinary benign data with coherence checks is needed. Two of the tested sub-1B chat models start high: a Bio compliance fraction of 0.74 for Qwen2.5-0.5B (arXiv:2507.11544#r46) and 83.2% SORRY-Bench adversarial compliance for Qwen3-0.6B (arXiv:2606.28843#H21). Model-specific untreated comparisons above 100B are still needed.

source.title: Fine-tuning aligned language models compromises safety
source.authors: Xiangyu Qi; Yi Zeng; Tinghao Xie; Pin-Yu Chen; Ruoxi Jia; Prateek Mittal; Peter Henderson

original_result.setup: They fine-tuned GPT-3.5 Turbo and Llama-2-7b-Chat for one epoch on Alpaca or Dolly with safety-related examples removed, then had a GPT-4 judge score answers to 330 harmful instructions.
original_result.result: With Alpaca, the share of answers scored maximally harmful rose from 5.5% to 31.8% on GPT-3.5 Turbo and from 0.3% to 16.1% on Llama-2-7b-Chat; with Dolly, it rose from 4.5% to 23.9% and from 0.6% to 12.1%. Parameter-efficient tuning on Alpaca (LoRA, LLaMA-Adapter, prefix tuning) raised Llama-2-7b-Chat's share to 13.9-26.4%, while a separate AdvBench test scored by keyword matching found the Alpaca-tuned Llama-2-7b-Chat's attack success rising only from 0% before tuning to 5.2%.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A controlled ordinary-versus-damage-selected benign-data comparison above 100B, with matched untreated baselines and separately reported harmful-compliance effects.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V2.studies_by_size and versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.training.by_size include >100B, so large-model testing is present. However, arXiv:2410.10343#r17 and #r18 lack numerical untreated baselines; arXiv:2507.11544's untested-parts line excludes deliberately selected benign data; arXiv:2610.14937#r1 and #r2 pool models and its untested-parts line notes missing per-model values; arXiv:2608.21727#r8 and #r9 concern factual RLVR and targeted PII extraction. No supplied part covers the matched comparison.

untested.what: Damage-maximizing benign-subset selection combined with matched multilingual safety evaluation.

The selected-data studies supply no corresponding multilingual evaluation matrix. counts: versions.V2.coverage_by_operation.training.by_family establishes broad family coverage but provides no selection-by-language cross-tab; the gap rests on the pack descriptions, not an absence of multilingual tests.

wording_issues.issue: An unconditional directional reading does not fit preserved or improved safety. Random 100-example subsets leave Llama-2-7B-Chat GPT-4 harmfulness at 1.13±0.08 (Dolly) and 1.21±0.11 (Alpaca) versus 1.18±0.14 untreated. MATH/TACO full SFT raises harmful-request refusal by 11.3 and 10.5 percentage points on Llama3.2-3B and Llama3.1-8B, while the same recipe lowers Qwen3-1.7B refusal by 13.5 points (one training seed per setting). Qwen3.5-4B WikiQA and MedQA SFT raise HarmBench refusal from 97.0% to 100.0% and from 95.0% to 99.5%. Secure-code GPT-4o tuning leaves StrongREJECT refusal at 99.0%, matching untreated (verdict/text only); insecure-code tuning gives 98.1%, a small decrease the check classes as partial rather than absent. The claim needs a conditional reading tied to model, data, training and evaluation.

Selection does not fix the direction. DataShield's lowest-risk 1,000-example Alpaca subsets lower Llama3-8B DirectHarm4 ASR from 12.75% to 1.50% and HEx-PHI from 5.86% to 0.34%, though Qwen2.5 Dolly DirectHarm4 and HarmBench rise slightly, 9.50%→10.20% and 6.50%→8.50%. Lowest-LARF Alpaca lowers Llama3 DirectHarm4 ASR from 11.25% to 0.75%. Low-risk recursive-distillation prompts lower Qwen3 14B SORRY-Bench compliance from 0.31 to 0.28 off-policy and 0.23 on-policy; the check's notes on the same appendix report Phi-4 14B rising from 0.26 to 0.55 and 0.47 under that selection (no extracted row). Acoustic audio selection lowers AdvBench JSR for AF3 (7.69% to 2.88–3.65%) and for Kimi-Audio at 50% (4.62% to 1.54%), but Kimi acoustic selection at 75% raises it to 19.23% (from the check, no row). The claim would need to name the selection objective, construction, dose, model and training procedure.

Benign prompts, safe answers to harmful prompts, explicit refusals and identity-shifting instructions are different interventions. Durability's AOA identity-shift set is 100 examples without malicious instructions, described as benign QA with a shifted persona and tone, that trains an affirmative prefix; its verdict counts it as V2 support while noting it is a distinct intervention. Safety Gap uses PKU-SafeRLHF safe-response subsets that include explicit refusals. Recursive distillation can train on safe self-answers to harmful prompts, and later recursive generations can become unsafe, so its training targets are not guaranteed benign. Erasure retraining uses a harmful-topic forget subset: the paper calls the attack benign but does not establish the subset's benign status.

wording_issues.phrase: ordinary or carefully chosen benign data
wording_issues.issue: Some supporting interventions engineer responses, stages or objectives rather than select ordinary benign examples: refusal overfitting followed by benign answers, refusal-prefixed SFT, benign DPO with refusal dispreferred, and deliberately false-answer training. In the two-stage study, removing the refusal-overfitting stage leaves Llama2-7b ASR at 4.42% after the ten ordinary stage-two pairs, with no matched untreated baseline; the check reads this ablation as an absent effect (challenges), not limits_scope. These constructions should keep their own labels and not stand for ordinary benign data.

The evidence mixes verified harmful output with non-refusal, ordinal harmfulness, pairwise harmlessness preference and composite safety. After Alpaca tuning, Granite Guardian 3.0-2B compliance stays at 0% while outputs become 100% ambiguous/incoherent; the check reads this as no compliance increase (challenges), not limits_scope. LLM-only OmniAlign-V tuning raises Qwen-2-VL-7B's no-attack non-refusal rate from 0.38% to 45.38%, but this rate counts any non-refusal and harmfulness is not measured. SafeAnchor's composite of HarmBench refusal, TruthfulQA and inverted BBQ falls from 91.4 to 43.6 ± 2.1 on Llama-2-7B-Chat, with components not reported separately. For both of these the check sets the V2 state to cannot_determine and the verdict to none. The fusion study measures pairwise harmlessness preference.

An increase can depend on the attack wrapper or benchmark. In the Representation Engineering study, benign tuning leaves plain direct-prompt ASR at baseline level on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-14B (the check reads this as challenges), while AIM and refusal-suppression wrappers raise ASR; direct prompting on Qwen2.5-1.5B does increase. The ISA increase (GPT-ASR 56%→100% on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 48%→96% on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, 500 ISA-templated benign samples) is measured only on ISA-transformed prompts. Generic benign data and plain-prompt evaluation are untested, so no comparison shows that the effect depends on template matching. Diffusion safe-subset SFT worsens direct compliance while improving several attacked conditions. Benign Alpaca LoRA raises Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct HarmBench compliance from .055 to .149 [.101,.197] but lowers StrongREJECT harmfulness from .054 to .039 [.030,.049] (text, Table 1).

A post-tuning level alone does not measure an increase, and a before/after difference does not isolate benign training. Locking Down reports post-Alpaca (50,000 examples) HEx-PHI harmfulness for Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B and Mistral-Large-2 without numerical untreated baselines; its 'Vanilla' column is an already fine-tuned model. The later DataShield reports Phi3-medium standard-SFT HEx-PHI ASR of 62.0% after Alpaca and 64.5% after Dolly, with no numerical pre-tuning ASR. Downloaded Qwen3-14B and Gemma3-12B-it adapter pools are compared with their source models, but the adapters' training data are not established as benign; the check gives these pools no V2 verdict. The UltraMedical-versus-backbone comparison does not report detailed training data or example counts; the study attributes the training to medical corpora without explicit safety constraints. These are distinct from controlled before/after benign-tuning experiments.

The records go beyond supervised adaptation of a standalone chat model. They include DPO on unsafe SORRY-Bench prompts with refusal-preferred pairs: training only on pairs where both candidates refuse still lowers refusal (qualitative), while the full preference set also contains pairs where both candidates are non-refusals. They also include continual pretraining followed by instruction tuning; self-play RL, where AZR-Coder-3B ASR Avg rises from 15.6 to 24.1 at step 130 while HarmBench ASR stays at 13.8; and supervised latent-link training between frozen agents. These operations test different interventions and should keep their own operation labels.

Some records do not establish erosion of safety the model already had, or need capability context. The open checkpoints in the self-generation study may be base models. TamperBench pools training stages. The PEFT study's 235 conversational runs include Mistral, which has no safety-specific fine-tuning: the check gives Mistral's own results no V2 verdict, and reads the pooled aggregate, a non-significant decrease, as challenges. On Qwen3-0.6B, falling multilingual harmful compliance comes with suspected model collapse.

method_sensitivity.what: Llama-2-7B-chat GSM8K ASR is 18.08 ± 2.49% with chat:llama training/testing versus 1.08 ± 0.12% with chat:vanilla training and chat:llama testing; the matched untreated chat:llama baseline is 0.00%. GPT-3.5 BookCorpus tuning lowers harmfulness under a suffix, 63.7%→54.8%, but raises it without the suffix, 12.7%→26.2%. Dolly KD is substantially more damaging with a chat student template than non-chat; teacher-only chat KD largely preserves baseline safety. Alpaca adaptation can increase wrapper-based vulnerability while direct-prompt ASR stays near baseline.

method_sensitivity.factor: Benchmark, judge, metric and output coherence
method_sensitivity.what: Qwen2.5-7B AdvBench refusal changes from 93.0% to 58.2% under regex judging but to 85.2% under Llama-Guard-3-8B; StrongReject shows no meaningful erosion under either judge. Controlled medical tuning improves MedSafetyBench safety by a median 12.2 percentage points while worsening MLCommons by a median 26.4 points. Granite Guardian Alpaca tuning leaves compliance at 0% while producing 100% ambiguous/incoherent outputs. Capability-grounded evaluation attributes large Qwen ARC harmfulness jumps to incoherent outputs misjudged by LlamaGuard.

Random 100-example Dolly/Alpaca subsets give Llama-2-7B-Chat harmfulness scores of 1.13±0.08 and 1.21±0.11 versus 1.18±0.14 untreated, while Self-Inf-N influence-selected subsets give 3.47±0.26 and 3.71±0.10 (1–5 scale). Lowest-LARF subsets can reduce ASR even when highest-LARF subsets raise it. On Qwen2-7B, Bi-Anchor versus Self-Inf-N selection gives mean harmfulness (1–5 scale) of 2.57 versus 1.84 against 1.69 untreated. In the SafeOff study's keyword-placement table on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (ADVBench ASR fractions, one seed per cell, untreated 0.01), two and four scattered safety keywords give 0.32 and 0.69; one prefix keyword gives 0.13, and fixed-position cells at any count or a single scattered keyword stay within 0.05–0.17. Position and keyword count both vary across these cells. Selection criterion and response construction therefore specify different interventions.

method_sensitivity.factor: Full tuning, PEFT family, objective and permitted parameters
method_sensitivity.what: On Llama-3.1-8B with 100 Alpaca examples, full SFT gives 75.40% HEx-PHI ASR and rank-32 LoRA 2.40% against 6.20% untreated. UltraFeedback LoRA produces aggregate safety gains of +4.925/+6.086/+7.096 percentage points at ranks 4/8/16, while prompt-based PEFT can lose safety; the aggregate includes a model lacking safety alignment. MATH/TACO SFT and GRPO-based RLVR have different model-specific safety effects. Restricting updates to the lowest-ESI 10% of weights leaves Llama3-8B AGNews HarmBench ASR at 15.8% versus 15.0% untreated, classified negligible.

method_sensitivity.factor: Learning rate, exposure, checkpoint and sequential order
method_sensitivity.what: Llama-3.1-8B GSM8K LoRA unsafe completions remain below the 2.8% untreated anchor through step 100, reaching 2.3 ± 0.4%, although Alpaca full tuning raises them. In DART tuning of that model, coherent-ASR fractions are 0.28 ± 0.03, 0.50 ± 0.11 and 0.29 ± 0.05 at learning rates 2e-5, 5e-5 and 1e-4, respectively, against 0.27 untreated; the highest rate degrades quality. In DataRx's LoRA task tuning (figure-only values), Llama3 and Qwen2.5 show a smaller ASR increase at learning rate 2e-5 than at 2e-4, but Mistral degrades substantially even at 2e-5. Sequential task order changes endpoint ASR and allows partial recovery at later stages.

method_sensitivity.factor: Response source, refusal targets and preference curation
method_sensitivity.what: Human-response Dolly tuning raises Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct plain-RefusalBench mean harmfulness from 1.18 to 3.11; synthetic single- and multi-source responses give 1.27 and 1.21 (reported average increase 0.06). GPT-4o benign DPO reaches ASR 59.13 ± 1.24% with refusal dispreferred versus 21.00 ± 0.91% with a non-refusal dispreferred; these are alternative post-training conditions. In on-policy SORRY-Bench DPO on Gemma-2B-IT and Llama-3-8B-Instruct, training only on pairs whose two responses are both refusals still lowers refusal, while gold human-labelled refusal-preferred pairs cause no unalignment; an added SFT term prevents refusal loss on the original mixed dataset, which also contains pairs of two non-refusals. These DPO outcomes are stated in prose, with rates figure-only. Removing boundary refusals from multilingual distillation lowers MultiJail JSR from 12.5% to 5.9% on Llama-3-8B and 5.7% to 4.03% on Qwen3-8B.

method_sensitivity.factor: Initial safety training and protection during adaptation
method_sensitivity.what: Ultra Chat tuning changes harmful-response proportions by −0.02 to +0.02 on seven refusal-robust Llama-3-8B variants (DERTA and RT2 −0.02; RT3 +0.02; RR, LAT, TAR and RT1 0), versus +0.75 on ordinary Llama-3-8B-Instruct. Freezing identified safety-critical weights lowers Llama2-7B-chat ASRVanilla after 10 Alpaca examples from 0.53 unfrozen to 0.23, but after 100 examples only from 0.94 to 0.89; untuned ASRVanilla is approximately 0 (all proportions). Under one-epoch GSM8K adaptation, safety-pretrained SafeLM-1.7B average ASR changes from 0.16% to 0.80%, compared with SafePost's 2.58% to 14.16%. MMAligner-defended multimodal models retain higher refusal after benign adaptation than comparator defenses, although some erosion remains.

method_sensitivity.factor: Model family, scale and teacher–student pairing
method_sensitivity.what: AM-DeepSeek reasoning LoRA SFT raises Qwen2.5-3B/7B HEx-PHI harmfulness from 10.00% to 20.33% and 13.33% to 25.33%, but lowers Gemma-3-4B's from 12.67% to 5.00% (24,337 training examples); the Ministral-3-3B and two Qwen2.5-14B runs show no increase, two of them decreasing in point estimates (34.00%→30.67%, 7.00%→4.67%; significance not established). In that study, cross-family runs differ in training size and model-specific settings. Imprinting raises Qwen2.5-7B compliance, whereas a Qwen3-32B base teacher lowers Ministral-8B SORRY fulfillment fraction from 0.6795 to 0.5773. SAFETUNE code tuning has negligible Qwen erosion but substantial L3 erosion under its fixed recipe. Safety Gap's safe-response tuning can reduce compliance on small Qwen models despite increases in its larger supporting conditions.

method_sensitivity.factor: Language, modality, style and social-pressure context
method_sensitivity.what: For Llama-3.2-1B Hindi tuning/evaluation, compliance is 25.3% at LoRA α/r=2 and 13.7% at α/r=8 against 23.0% untreated; English versus matching-language evaluation also changes direction across models. Acoustic-selected SD-QA audio tuning lowers AF3 AdvBench JSR from 7.69% to 2.88% at 25% or 50% fractions despite increases in other selection conditions. With list-prefix test queries, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct tuning on 1,000 list-prefix-styled examples raises ASR more than tuning on the 1,000 style-removed pairs, and mixing in style-removed data largely mitigates the increase (figure-only values); some model–style pairs are exceptions. Ordinary SFT on sycophancy-plus-Alpaca data lowers Qwen3.5-9B-Base direct refusal from 87.2% (258/296) to 78.4% (232/296) and pressure-suffix refusal from 90.9% (269/296) to 65.5% (194/296), a reported 25.3 percentage-point decrease; this starting checkpoint is not a shipped safety-trained chat model.

method_sensitivity.factor: Recursive teachers, training objective and communication topology
method_sensitivity.what: Recursive self-distillation (RSD) outcomes depend on the evolving teacher, on/off-policy training and prompt selection. Safe-answer SFT and frozen-teacher controls remove the evolving teacher and show no erosion like RSD's; RSD on random benign prompts keeps the evolving teacher but changes prompt selection, and also shows no misalignment. Low-risk selected Qwen3-14B curricula lower SORRY-Bench compliance fractions from 0.31 initially to 0.28 off-policy and 0.23 on-policy. Latent-link RL gives Mixture-system mean compliance score 5.7 versus text communication's 12.5, while supervised links can worsen safety. AZR-7B self-evolution, evaluated at step 350, lowers HarmBench ASR from 23.5 to 11.5 and average ASR from 20.9 to 19.7; EVOL-RL produces substantial refusal loss on its tested instruct models.

status_amendment.public_note: The rating changed from contested to independently reproduced under specified training recipes: several independent groups that fine-tuned Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5 on Alpaca data (the full set or 1,000-example subsets) found the same rise in harmful outputs, usually smaller, while two that used shorter or more conservative training on Llama-2-7B-Chat found none, and we found no failed matched replication and no paper showing the rise as a whole to be a measurement artifact. Other tests also find no erosion in specific conditions, such as some LoRA settings, small random data subsets, GPT-4 and GPT-4o, and some judges, and below 1B parameters the evidence is too thin to rate.
status_amendment.level_changed_because: C to R2 under specified recipes with scope limits. The previous C rested on challenges verdicts in tested conditions, not on a failed replication or a credible artifact argument. Part of its <1B basis was safe-response tuning whose data include explicit refusals (arXiv:2507.11544#r46; arXiv:2507.11544#r47). The README defines C as a failed replication or a credible artifact paper, and neither is established in the evidence: the closest independent nulls on Llama-2-7B-Chat with Alpaca data (arXiv:2608.26506#benign-llama2-7b; arXiv:2505.12186#R51) differ from the original in recipe and metric. The clearest artifact-type argument, arXiv:2606.03648's judge and coherence account, carries a limits_scope verdict for the conditions it covers. Several independent near-original reruns on Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5 Turbo reproduce the direction, usually with smaller increases, and none of their studies shares authors with an original (arXiv:2405.14577#R9; arXiv:2505.06843#r7; arXiv:2410.00451#r27; arXiv:2410.00451#r37; arXiv:2312.14302#r21). The level is therefore R2, and the challenges verdicts limit its scope. The critic's next step leaves the choice between C and this R2 to Iris.
